The test image shows a split soybean stem with white/gray internal pith tissue. The pith appears whitened and somewhat shredded/fibrous. Key candidates: White Mold, Charcoal Rot, Brown Stem Rot.

Let me view reference images starting with these top candidates.
Now let me check the remaining classes systematically.

Based on all reference images viewed, I can now make my assessment.

**Key observations from test image:**
- Split soybean stem showing internal pith
- Very white/light gray pith tissue, fibrous and somewhat shredded in appearance
- Dark discoloration at stem outer edges
- Dry/late-season background context

**Comparison with references:**
- **Brown Stem Rot** (Dise_103): Shows clearly brown pith - much darker than test image
- **Charcoal Rot** (Dise_116): Shows gray pith with tiny black microsclerotia dots - test image is whiter and lacks visible dots
- **White Mold** (Dise_133): Shows dark sclerotia externally, but White Mold characteristically bleaches the stem white/gray internally with shredded cottony pith - matches the test image best
- All other classes (bacterial, leaf-spot, rust, virus) show foliar or root symptoms unrelated to the split stem with white pith

The very pale white/gray, fibrous, shredded pith visible in the split stem is the hallmark sign of **White Mold** (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum), which colonizes and bleaches the internal pith tissue while shredding its structure.
